5001:
Using \beta^2-\alpha^2=(\beta-\alpha)(\beta+\alpha) gives \beta+\alpha=3i
Since (\beta-\alpha)^2=(\beta+\alpha)^2-4\alpha\beta gives 11=-9-4\alpha\beta so \alpha\beta=-5
Writing \beta^3-\alpha^3=(\beta-\alpha)[(\beta-\alpha)^2+3\alpha\beta] gives \sqrt{11}(11-15)=-4\sqrt{11}
Squaring gives 16 \times 11=176 → (B)
5002:
For an A.P. with sum S_{n}=3n^2+5n the term is T_{n}=S_{n}-S_{n-1}=6n+2
Hence T_{n}^2=(6n+2)^2=36n^2+24n+4
Summing with \sum n=55 and \sum n^2=385 gives 36 \times 385+24 \times 55+40=15220 → (C)
5003:
Reading the action on e_{3} and e_{1}+e_{3} gives the first and third columns of A while the transpose conditions fix the middle entry
Thus A has columns (2,1,3) and (1,3,1) with middle column (1,2,1) which indeed has \det(A)=1
Then A+I has determinant 8 so \det(A^2+A)=\det(A)\det(A+I)=8
For a 3 \times 3 matrix \det(\text{adj} M)=(\det M)^2 so 8^2=64 → (D)
5008:
Adding frequencies gives N=26 and total 234 so mean \bar{x}=9
Summing f_{i}|x_{i}-\bar{x}| gives 32+12+0+2+6+36=88
Dividing by N gives \frac{88}{26}=\frac{44}{13} → (C)
5010:
Completing squares gives circle centre (3,4) with radius 2 and parabola vertex (-3,-4)
Joining centre to vertex gives distance \sqrt{36+64}=10
Adding the radius outwards gives maximum 10+2=12 → (C)
5011:
In an equilateral triangle orthocentre and centroid coincide on the altitude from P
Projecting P(3,5) onto x+y=4 gives foot (1,3) so altitude vector is (-2,-2)
Moving two thirds along gives (\alpha,\beta)=(\frac{5}{3},\frac{11}{3}) so 9(\alpha+\beta)=48 → (D)
5012:
Rewriting with t=\cos x gives p=-3t^2+12t on t \in [-1,1]
Since the parabola vertex at t=2 lies right of the interval the range is from -15 to 9
Adding integers -15 through 9 gives -120+45=-75 → (C)
5013:
Taking A=(2,5,2) on the line gives AP=(3,1,5) with direction d=(2,3,4)
Projecting gives AP \cdot d=29 and |d|^2=29 while |AP|^2=35
Subtracting gives squared distance 35-\frac{29^2}{29}=6 → (C)
5015:
Equating coordinates forces the second line parameter \mu=0 from the z equation since a\neq 0
Then the first line gives \lambda=1 from y and a=3 from x with common point (4,0,-1)
Squaring distance from the origin gives 16+0+1=17 → (C)
5016:
Intersecting y=x^2 with xy=27 gives x=3 and y=9 dividing the range at x=3
Integrating gives area \int_{1}^{3}(x^2-1)dx+\int_{3}^{27}(\frac{27}{x}-1)dx
Evaluating gives 54\ln 3-\frac{52}{3} → (B)
5017:
Expanding \cos(\alpha x)\cos((\alpha+1)x)\cos((\alpha+2)x) to second order gives numerator \frac{\alpha^2+(\alpha+1)^2+(\alpha+2)^2}{2}x^2
Dividing by (\alpha+1)^2x^2 gives limit \frac{3\alpha^2+6\alpha+5}{2(\alpha+1)^2}=2 with \alpha\neq -1
Clearing gives \alpha^2+2\alpha-1=0 whose product is -1 → (C)
5018:
Substituting x=2\tan \theta with dx=2\sec^2\theta d\theta turns the integral into \frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\ln(2\tan \theta)d\theta
Splitting the logarithm leaves \frac{\pi}{4}\ln 2 plus \frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\ln(\tan \theta)d\theta which vanishes by symmetry
Hence the value is \frac{\pi \ln 2}{4} → (B)
5019:
Putting y=0 gives f(0)=0 and f(\frac{x}{3})=\frac{f(x)}{3} so f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y) making f additive
With differentiability and f'(0)=3 this forces f(x)=3x so g(x)=3+3xe^x
Differentiating gives g'(x)=3e^x(1+x) with minimum at x=-1 giving 3-\frac{3}{e}=3(\frac{e-1}{e}) → (B)
5020:
Rewriting the integrand as 3\sec^4 x-\sec^2 x\csc^2 x gives 2\sec^2 x+3\tan^2 x\sec^2 x-\csc^2 x
Integrating termwise gives antiderivative 2\tan x+\tan^3 x+\cot x
Evaluating from \frac{\pi}{6} to \frac{\pi}{3} gives \frac{16}{\sqrt{3}}-\frac{16}{3\sqrt{3}}=\frac{32}{3\sqrt{3}} → (C)
5021:
Constraining f(2)+f(3)=5 leaves pairs (1,4) and (4,1) and (2,3) and (3,2) all with f(3) \leq 4
Fixing any such pair leaves 3 admissible values for f(1) \geq 3 distinct from the pair
Permuting the remaining 3 values in 6 ways gives 4 \times 3 \times 6=72 → (72)
5025:
Substituting y=vx gives x\frac{dv}{dx}=-\frac{1}{\sin v} so \cos(\frac{y}{x})=\ln x with \cos(\frac{\pi}{2})=0
Putting x=e^{12} gives \alpha=\ln(e^{12})=12 turning the locus into x^2+y^2-2px+2py+14=0
Requiring radius \sqrt{2p^2-14} below or equal to 6 with positivity gives p^2 above 7 and at most 25 leaving \pm 3 and \pm 4 and \pm 5 → (6)
5026:
Vernier least count is LC = 1 MSD - 1 VSD = 1 mm - 0.9 mm = 0.1 mm = 0.01 cm
Vernier zero lies to the right of main scale zero so the zero error is positive
Coinciding division is 7 so error = 7 \times LC = 7 \times 0.01 cm = 0.07 cm
Positive error of 0.07 cm → (C)
5028:
For depth d the value is g_d = g(1 - d/R) and for small height h it is g_h = g(1 - 2h/R)
Here d = h = 16 km with R = 6400 km so fractional change is (g_d - g_h)/g = (2h - d)/R = 16/6400 = 0.0025
In percent this is 0.0025 \times 100 = 0.25 → (B)
5029:
Left side mass is m_1 = 4 kg and right side carries m_2 + m_3 = 10 kg so the right side moves down
System acceleration is a = (10g - 4g)/(4 + 4 + 6) = 6g/14 = 3g/7
For the left mass T_1 - m_1 g = m_1 a gives T_1 = 40g/7 and for m_3 alone m_3 g - T_2 = m_3 a gives T_2 = 24g/7
Hence T_1/T_2 = 40/24 = 5/3 → (A)
5030:
Let the wedge acquire acceleration A to the right under the pull f
In frictionless sliding the relative acceleration down the slope is a_{rel} = g \sin 37^{\circ} - A \cos 37^{\circ} with \sin 37^{\circ} = 0.6 and \cos 37^{\circ} = 0.8
With A = f/(M + m) = 24/12 = 2 m/s^{2} this gives a_{rel} = 10 \times 0.6 - 2 \times 0.8 = 4.4 m/s^{2}
From s = \frac{1}{2} a_{rel} t^{2} with s = 8.8 m, t = \sqrt{2 \times 8.8/4.4} = 2 s → (A)
5031:
Young modulus Y is a property of the material of the wire
It does not depend on length L or radius r which only enter the extension
Doubling both leaves Y unchanged → (C)
5032:
Internal energy change for an ideal gas is \Delta U = n C_v (T_f - T_i) with C_v = R/(\gamma - 1)
Adiabatic index is related to degrees of freedom f by \gamma = 1 + 2/f
Both statements are true but the second alone does not derive the first → (B)
5033:
Zeroth law defines temperature and first law defines internal energy so A and B are true
For isothermal expansion of an ideal gas \Delta U = 0 so \Delta Q = \Delta W and C is false
Product of intensive and extensive is extensive so D is true while specific ratio is intensive so E is false
Hence A, B and D only → (C)
5034:
Apply Kirchhoff laws to the diamond with the 10 V branch and the 5 V branch
Nodal analysis on the top and bottom nodes with 4 \Omega, 2 \Omega, 2 \Omega and 1 \Omega branches gives the branch distribution
The middle 1 \Omega branch carries I_1 = 2.5 A while the two symmetric side branches each carry 1.875 A
Hence I_1 = 2.5 A, I_2 = 1.875 A, I_3 = 1.875 A → (A)
5035:
Force on electron is \vec{F} = -e \vec{E} = -e(-2E_0 \hat{i}) = 2eE_0 \hat{i}
Acceleration is a = 2eE_0/m so velocity at time t is v = v_0 + 2E_0 e t/m
de Broglie wavelength is \lambda = h/(m v) = h/(m v_0 + 2E_0 e t) = 4 \lambda_0/[1 + 2E_0 e t/(m v_0)]
With \lambda_0 = h/(4 m v_0) this is the quoted form → (C)
5036:
Orbital radius scales as r \propto n^{2} so n_i/n_f = \sqrt{r_i/r_f} = \sqrt{16/4} = 2
This is the 4 \rightarrow 2 Balmer transition of H with 1/\lambda = R_H(1/4 - 1/16) = 3R_H/16
With R_H = 1.0973 \times 10^{7} m^{-1}, \lambda = 486 nm → (C)
5037:
Displacement current equals conduction current for charging, I_d = C dV/dt
Hence dV/dt = I_d/C = 4.0/(6 \times 10^{-6}) = 0.67 \times 10^{6} V/s
So \alpha = 0.67 → (B)
5038:
Each of the three upper rows has three 5 V sources in series with three 3 \Omega resistors giving 15 V and 9 \Omega per row
Three such rows in parallel are equivalent to 15 V with 9/3 = 3 \Omega in parallel with the lower 9 \Omega branch
Let V be the voltage between A and B, then 3(V - 15)/9 + V/9 = 0 gives V = 11.25 V
Current in the lower 9 \Omega branch is V/9 = 1.25 A → (B)
5039:
Fringe width is \beta = \lambda D/d and in a medium wavelength becomes \lambda/\mu
Hence width scales as \beta' = \beta/\mu = 2.4/1.2 = 2.0 \mu m
So the width is 2.0 \mu m → (B)
5041:
Photon energy is E = h c/\lambda = 6.0 \times 10^{-19} J for \lambda = 331 nm
Electron kinetic energy is K = eV_0 = 0.32 \times 10^{-19} J for stopping potential 0.2 V
Work function is W_0 = E - K = 5.68 \times 10^{-19} J so \alpha = 5.68 → (C)
5042:

Objective magnification is tube length divided by focal length, m_0 = L/f_0
To keep m_0 fixed at fixed object distance with 2f_0 the tube length must double → (A)
5044:
Let X_C = 1/(\omega C) be the reactance at frequency \omega with impedance Z_1 = \sqrt{R^{2} + X_C^{2}} and current I = V/Z_1
At frequency \omega/4 the reactance is 4X_C with Z_2 = \sqrt{R^{2} + 16X_C^{2}} and current I/3 = V/Z_2 so Z_2 = 3Z_1

5045:
First gate is OR so LED-1 follows A + B and glows when A + B = 1
Middle gate is AND of that output with C and final gate is AND of A with that result so LED-2 follows A(A + B)C = AC

5047:
Let y be the fallen distance with v^{2} = 2gy for free fall from rest
Setting magnitude v = g = 10 m/s gives 100 = 20y so y = 5 m
Height above ground is 18 - 5 = 13 m → (13)
5048:
Standard form is y = A \sin(\omega t + kx + \phi) so successive crests are separated by wavelength \lambda = 2\pi/k
Here k = 0.018 cm^{-1} so \lambda = 2 \times 3.14/0.018 = 348.88 cm

5049:
Magnetic force is always perpendicular to field so acceleration satisfies \vec{a} \cdot \vec{B} = 0
With \vec{B} = 3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} and \vec{a} = 4\hat{i} - (x/2)\hat{j}, dot product is 12 - x = 0
Hence x = 12 → (12)
5050:
L_1 carries total current I which splits equally as I/2 in identical parallel branches L_2 and L_3
Stored energies are U_1 = \frac{1}{2} L I^{2} and U_2 = U_3 = \frac{1}{2} L (I/2)^{2} = U_1/4

5052:
Ordering follows (n+l) rule with lower n first on ties
Sums are 3 for E, 4 for B, 5 for A, 6 for D and 7 for C
So increasing energy is E < B < A < D < C → (D)
5053:

Orbital size grows with n so 2p is smaller than 3p, and Cr is [\text{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{1} from half-filled stability
Energy of 2s depends on Z, so 2s of H differs from 2s of Li and C is false → (B)
5056:
Mixture A has 4 \text{ mmol} base versus 2.5 \text{ mmol} acid, so basic
Mixture B has equal acid and base, so neutral, while C has excess acid, so acidic
Hence pH order is C < B < A → (C)
5058:
Electronegativity follows F > O > N across the period
In \text{OF}_{2} F is -1 giving O as +2, and in \text{Na}_{2}\text{O} Na is +1 giving O as -2
Both statements are true → (A)
5060:
Interstitial compounds keep metallic conductivity with high melting points and inert non-stoichiometric character
They are very hard and not ionic in nature

5062:

Ligand field removes five-fold degeneracy of d orbitals
Both statements state correct crystal field principles → (A)
5066:
Reagent \text{AgCN} attacks through N, so benzyl bromide forms benzyl isocyanide
Carbylamine of benzylamine with \text{CHCl}_{3} and aqueous NaOH also gives benzyl isocyanide
Aryl halide with \text{AgCN} and alkyl bromide with KCN give different products, so only A and B work → (A)
5068:
Benzylamine is stronger base than aniline and p-nitrophenol from diazotization dissolves in NaOH, so A and D are true
Gabriel phthalimide fails for aryl halides, so p-anisidine cannot be made that way and B is false

Forms crystallize at 303 \text{ K} and 371 \text{ K}, so A, B and E are true

5070:

Phenolphthalein is a weak acid \text{HPh} ionizing in basic medium rather than a weak base in acidic medium
